title: Week 7 - Privacy
content: # Privacy in Blockchains ### Privacy in BTC & ETH #### ETH Everyone can see: - Addresses and their balances - Contract state - Call data - Events / logs Privacy is a priority for ETH: - Stealth Address was done in ERC-5564 - Creation of the Privacy Stewards of Ethereum (PSE) & Ethereum Foundation Privacy Roadmap - To incentivize developers to build features with selective disclosure in Ethereum. #### BTC You can be pseudonymous. The privacy is partial and fragile. - Address reuse enables traceability - Graphs & other heuristics can be used to link inputs and outputs ### Know Your Customer (KYC) In many jurisdictions, some services are required to collect customer identification. - Centralized Exchanges - On-Ramp and Off-Ramp Services ## Major Privacy Approaches ### Bitcoin CoinJoin - Concept of Mixer Multiple users combine inputs in one transaction. - This is still vulnerable to graph and heuristics but it blurs things #### ETH Mixer Implemented as a smart contract and uses ZK proofs with a commitment and nullifier scheme. ### SGX-Based Privacy Encrypt information on the blockchain and use special hardware to decrypt and compute data. - Validators use hardware-based security technology to isolate sensitive code and data in protected, encrypted memory regions called enclaves. **Pro**: Prevents validators from dumping the memory and looking at the data **Cons**: Requires complex key distribution and is prone to hardware vulnerabilities. ### Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) A cryptographic technique allowing computations to be performed on encrypted data without decrypting it. - No need for specialized hardware - Only allows for a limited set of operations ### Monero The coin of choice for illegal activity. It has the following features: 1. Ring Signatures 1. Hide sender among N decoys 2. Stealth Addresses 1. One-time receiver addresses 3. Confidential Transactions 1. Uses a ZK proof with a commitment
